newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: ARGENTINE BONDS HIGHER, BOOSTED BY RUSSIAN MARKETS.
newsitem.headline: ARGENTINE BONDS HIGHER, BOOSTED BY RUSSIAN MARKETS.

text.p: Argentine bonds were higher late morning Thursday, boosted by general strength in emerging debt markets on the back of signs that Russia is nearing a deal to restructure its commercial debt.
Traders predicted that with international market conditions continuing to be supportive, Argentine spreads will tighten more.
"The market is firm, I continue to have a strong outlook for the medium-term," said the head trader at a foreign bank.
Argentina's Par Brady bond was up 1/4 at 75-1/8, while the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 was up $0.03 at 119.05.
But traders stressed that the market was just tracking other emerging markets and U.S. Treasuries with no specific Argentine news pushing prices.
"Trade is pretty thin," said another trader.
